What American Curriculum Students Need

Five academic needs that shape how an American Curriculum student moves from Grade 6 to AP.

Steady Pace

American Curriculum grades come weekly, so steady habits matter more than cramming.

GPA Watch

Grade 9 onwards, each course grade rolls into the GPA universities review.

Yearly Depth

Each grade level adds new content, so subject understanding must grow steadily.

Sharp Writing

FRQs and essays reward clear claims, strong evidence, and structured argument.

AP Mindset

AP needs independent revision, timed practice, and steady weekly synoptic review.

How Ustaad Supports American Curriculum Students

Each need above answered in lessons, from Grade 6 right through to the AP exam.

Continuous Pressure

Weekly quizzes, projects, and tests held steady so every grade lands cleanly.

GPA Awareness

From Grade 9, each course grade is protected because GPA starts counting then.

Free-Response Practice

Essays and FRQs marked the way College Board readers mark them in May.

AP-Ready Habits

Independent study, timed practice, and synoptic review built in before AP year.

American Curriculum schools operate across Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, and Umm Al Quwain. Every school grades on the same rolling system, so the same tutoring rhythm fits each district, but matching the lesson to the right unit each week is what holds the grade steady. Ustaad pairs each student with a tutor who knows the school, the grade level, and the current units. Sessions run online after school hours so the schedule fits family life rather than forcing it to fit the tutor.
